Neches River Near Alto affecting Houston, Angelina, Anderson and
Cherokee Counties.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Neches River near Alto.

* WHEN...From Friday morning to Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 16.0 feet, Boat ramps and picnic areas near the river
will begin to flood. Ranchers should move cattle and equipment near
the river to higher ground.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:15 AM CDT Thursday the stage was 4.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage Friday
morning to a crest of 16.4 feet early Saturday morning. It will
then fall below flood stage late Saturday evening.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

walking near riverbanks. Turn around, don't drown when encountering
flooded roads. Most flood deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

For more hydrologic information, copy and paste the following website
address into your favorite web browser URL bar:
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/SHV

The next statement will be issued Friday morning at 830 AM CDT.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 3 at 6:21PM EDT until September 3 at 8:30PM EDT by NWS Pittsburgh PA
properties.description:

heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 1.5 inches of rain
have fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Law enforcement reported.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor

Bessemer, Koppel, Wampum, South New Castle, New Galilee, Enon

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued September 3 at 7:29PM EDT until September 3 at 7:45PM EDT by NWS State College PA
properties.description:
At 729 PM EDT, severe thunderstorms were located along a line from
over Ehrenfeld to near New Centerville, or along a line from 5 miles
southeast of Nanty-Glo to 12 miles southwest of Somerset, moving
southeast at 35 mph.

HAZARD...70 mph wind gusts and small hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect considerable tree damage. Damage is likely to mobile
homes, roofs, and outbuildings.

Locations impacted include...
Johnstown, Somerset, Westmont, Windber, Ebensburg, Belmont,
Nanty-Glo, Portage, Geistown, Southmont, Berlin, Friedens, Vinco,
Boswell, Dale, East Conemaugh, Salix-Beauty Line Park, Davidsville
and Central City.

This includes The Pennsylvania Turnpike between mile markers 100 and
127.
properties.instruction:
Anyone outdoors should move to shelter inside a well-built structure
and stay away from windows. These storms are capable of producing
widespread damaging winds.

Tornadoes can develop quickly from severe thunderstorms. Seek shelter
immediately in an interior room on the lowest floor of a well-built
structure.

Continuous cloud to ground lightning is occurring with these storms.
Lightning is one of nature's leading killers. Remember, if you can
hear thunder, you are close enough to be struck by lightning.

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued September 3 at 7:35PM EDT until September 3 at 7:45PM EDT by NWS Pittsburgh PA
properties.description:
The storms which prompted the warning have weakened below severe
limits, and no longer pose an immediate threat to life or property.
Therefore, the warning will be allowed to expire. However, heavy rain
is still possible with these thunderstorms.

To report severe weather, contact your nearest law enforcement
agency. They will send your report to the National Weather Service
office.

A Severe Thunderstorm Watch remains in effect until 1000 PM EDT
Thursday for portions of northwest and western Pennsylvania.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 3 at 4:50PM CDT until September 5 at 4:28PM CDT by NWS Houston/Galveston TX
properties.description:
...Forecast flooding changed from Moderate to Major severity and
increased in duration for the following rivers in Texas...

Menard Creek near Rye affecting Polk, Hardin and Liberty Counties.

For the Menard Creek...including Rye...Major flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...Menard Creek near Rye.

* WHEN...Until Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 28.0 feet, Major lowland flooding begins with
widespread inundation of the floodplain in the vicinity of the
gage.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 4:15 PM CDT Thursday the stage was 27.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 17.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 4:15 PM CDT Thursday was 27.8 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 28.2 feet
this evening. It will then fall below flood stage early Saturday
morning.
- Flood stage is 20.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 28.2
feet on 04/21/1979.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/hgx.

The next statement will be issued Friday morning at 700 AM CDT.
